Constants depend on m,d,A and are ineffective.
needed: MN20 for the fixed nilsequence models entering the complexity20 prime theorem.
derivation: Specialize the published polynomial-nilsequence theorem to linear orbits in the degree20 filtration, as its printed p543 remark explicitly permits. source.statement: For a fixed arithmetic progression with coprime residue and modulus, the Mertens product has a positive constant and the prescribed reciprocal-logarithm exponent. In particular the two unit classes modulo4 have exponent1/2; removing finitely many fixed primes changes only the positive constant.

available: For ell different from the characteristic, Hom(E1,E2) tensor Z_ell injects into Hom(T_ell E1,T_ell E2).
needed: The rational centralizer of the defined order-four automorphism iota is exactly Q(i).
derivation: Use ell=3, which differs from p>324. The explicit Fp-defined iota has iota²=-1, so it embeds Q(i) into the rational endomorphism algebra. Tensor the rational centralizer with Q3 and use the Tate injection: its image lies in the centralizer of iota on a two-dimensional Q3-space. Because T²+1 is irreducible over Q3, that latter centralizer is Q3(i) of dimension2. The rational centralizer has dimension at most2 and contains Q(i), hence equals Q(i). The lower inclusion is essential; this does not assert the full geometric endomorphism algebra equals Q(i).
boundary: The actual good reduction, i in Fp and formula for iota are separate displayed local computations.

available: The q-power Frobenius satisfies a monic integral quadratic polynomial in End(E).
needed: The arithmetic p-power Frobenius, already in the rational centralizer Q(i), belongs to Z[i].
derivation: Coordinate p-power Frobenius commutes with (x,y)↦(-x,iy) because i is in Fp. The previously identified centralizer therefore contains this actual Frobenius. Its monic integral polynomial makes it integral over Z; the integer ring of Q(i) is Z[i], giving a+bi with integers a,b.
boundary: This does not assert all geometric endomorphisms belong to Q(i); only the centralizer and actual Frobenius do.

locator: III Proposition8.6,p99; V Theorem2.3.1 and proof,p142
available: On a prime-to-characteristic Tate module, determinant equals isogeny degree and trace equals1+degree(phi)−degree(1−phi). For q-power Frobenius the degree isq and degree(1−phi)=#E(Fq).
needed: Writing Frobenius as a+bi gives p=a²+b² and the two opposite-twist orders p+1±2a.
derivation: The Tate space is a one-dimensional Q3(i)-vector space, so a+bi has Q3-trace2a and determinant a²+b². Frobenius degree p and the degree(1−phi) point count give p=a²+b² and d1=p+1−2a. The actual two reductions are opposite squareclass quadratic twists by2341–2347, which negates the trace and gives d2=p+1+2a. This twist fact is a separate local computation, not supplied by the determinant theorem.
boundary: Opposite twists follow from product7 and the selected Legendre symbol; they are not an extra conclusion of the Tate determinant formula.

available_assertion.statement: For an imaginary quadratic order, the singular moduli are roots of a monic integral class polynomial, hence are algebraic integers.
available_assertion.objects: Classical elliptic singular moduli of imaginary quadratic orders.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The elliptic curve has geometric complex multiplication by an imaginary quadratic order.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every imaginary quadratic order, including nonmaximal orders.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Negative order discriminants; elliptic curves in characteristic zero.
available_assertion.uniformity: Algebraic integrality for all such singular moduli.
available_assertion.constants: No numerical height bound or discriminant estimate used.
available_assertion.normalizations: Use the classical elliptic Weierstrass c4^3/discriminant invariant and the full CM order, including nonmaximal orders.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No maximal-order restriction; this is not a formula for a quaternionic Hauptmodul.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix the CM order and form its class polynomial.

needed: The actual nonsingular E_ell with classical j=35152/9 has no geometric complex multiplication.
connecting_argument: If E_ell had geometric CM, its endomorphism order, not necessarily maximal, would make its classical elliptic j an algebraic integer by the monic integral order class polynomial. For a reduced rational a/b, multiplying a monic equation by b^n gives b dividing a^n, hence b=1. Here35152 is not divisible by3, so35152/9 is not integral. Contradiction.

retained_inputs.statement: The displayed nonsingular model has the computed classical j invariant; ell is nonzero.

boundary: This application does not supply open image, a uniform index, or any assertion about the distinct CM generator curve. The earlier derived non-CM output is not a premise.
